summary: Completes the target inventory of dimension, depth and complete intersections for patching, importing the existing depth, Cohen–Macaulay and support contracts and the native regular-sequence/projective-dimension APIs. This part adds finite minimal resolutions and Auslander–Buchsbaum, regular-sequence ideals, absolute local complete intersections and the precise scalar-restriction and flat-local formulas. The inherited Hilbert–Samuel proof leaves remain explicit.

nodes.title: Regular-sequence ideals
nodes.statement: For an ideal I of R, IsRegularSequenceIdeal I means that there is a finite list f of elements of R with Ideal.ofList f = I and RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R f. This is a property of the ideal, not of a chosen presentation. No Noetherian assumption is built into the predicate. The final quotient is nonzero, so the unit ideal is excluded; over a nonzero ring the zero ideal is represented by the empty list.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the native list regularity predicate and the native generated ideal; quantify over lists.
acceptance: The unit ideal is false, including in the zero ring.

sources.match: Local minimal generators preserve the regular-sequence property; this motivates an ideal-level predicate.
The kernel ideal, rather than a selected list, enters the local CI criterion.

uses.how: Recognize the kernel of a regular local presentation independently of its generators.
Apply a finite regular sequence as a specialization ideal.

nodes.title: Regular generators and codimension
nodes.statement: Let R be a Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay local ring, f a list in its maximal ideal and c=f.length. Then f is R-regular iff dim(R/Ideal.ofList f)+c=dim R. Equality is in extended dimension, with the finite local dimensions and proper ideal understood.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: The principal dimension bound forces every intermediate quotient to drop by exactly one when total drop is c.
Apply cm-parameter-element inductively; the reverse implication is the native regular-sequence dimension drop.
acceptance: No assertion is made for a non-CM ring or a list containing a unit.

sources.match: Full codimension in a CM module forces regularity; the ring specialization gives the criterion.

nodes.title: CM parameter elements
nodes.statement: Let M be a nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay module over a Noetherian local R. If x lies in the maximal ideal and dim Supp(M/xM)+1=dim Supp M, then multiplication by x on M is injective.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Every associated prime of CM M has quotient dimension dim Supp M by the supplier CM contract. If x were in such a prime, native support_quotSMulTop would put its full-dimensional closed support in Supp(M/xM), contradicting the dimension drop.
The native union-of-associated-primes characterization of zero divisors therefore makes x injective.
acceptance: For a zero-dimensional nonzero M no such x exists.

sources.match: The dimension drop makes x regular; the induction exchanges two parameter elements.

nodes.title: Minimal generators of regular ideals
nodes.statement: Over a Noetherian local R, suppose I is a regular-sequence ideal and f is a list of elements of I generating I whose residue classes form a basis of I/mI over the residue field. Then f is R-regular.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: A regular list gives a basis of I/I² by the supplier Koszul/conormal result, and hence of I/mI.
The change matrix between two minimal generating lists is invertible over R by Nakayama; transport Koszul exactness under its exterior-power automorphism.
Use the local equivalence between regularity and Koszul acyclicity from the same supplier contract; its precise comparison is requested.
acceptance: Redundant generators are deliberately excluded.
In the suggested signature, generation together with list length equal to the native ideal spanFinrank expresses the same residue-basis condition.

sources.match: The local equivalence and invariance under changing generators prove this statement.

nodes.title: Faithfully flat descent of regular ideals
nodes.statement: For a flat local map of Noetherian local rings R→S and proper ideal I of R, I is a regular-sequence ideal iff IS is a regular-sequence ideal.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Extend a minimal generating list of I; residue-field extension keeps it minimal for IS.
Use regular-sequence-ideal-minimal-generators and faithful reflection for the reverse direction; native faithful-flat ascent proves the forward direction.
acceptance: The adjective local is needed to turn flatness into faithful flatness here.

sources.match: Regularity of a fixed list is reflected and preserved by a flat local map.

sources.locator: §23.7, Lemma23.7.6, tag09PX, pp.18–19, final descent step
sources.match: A minimal generating list stays minimal under a flat local map, reducing descent of the ideal property to descent of list regularity.

nodes.title: Reflection of regular sequences
nodes.statement: If S is faithfully flat over R, then for any R-module M and list f, f is M-regular iff its image list is regular on S⊗R M.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Successive quotient modules commute with tensor product.
Faithful flatness reflects the zero kernel of each multiplication map and the nonzero final quotient.
acceptance: For M=0 both regularity assertions are false.

sources.match: This adds the converse to the pinned ascent API without redefining regularity.

nodes.title: Kernels between regular local rings
nodes.statement: If φ:R→S is a surjection of regular local rings, then ker φ is generated by a prefix of a regular system of parameters of R. In particular it is a regular-sequence ideal of length dim R−dim S.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Lift a basis of the kernel of m_R/m_R²→m_S/m_S² and extend it to a basis of the source.
The quotient by that prefix is regular of the same dimension as S, using the imported regular-parameter theorem.
A nonzero kernel in a regular local domain strictly lowers dimension, so the remaining surjection is an isomorphism.
acceptance: A surjection between equal-dimensional regular local rings is an isomorphism.

sources.match: Cotangent-space counting puts the kernel inside a regular parameter system.

nodes.title: Changing regular local presentations
nodes.statement: Given surjections R→S→A with R and S regular local and A nonzero local Noetherian, ker(R→A) is a regular-sequence ideal iff ker(S→A) is.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Choose a regular parameter prefix generating ker(R→S); lift minimal generators of ker(S→A).
The concatenated list generates ker(R→A), and the dimension-drop criterion proves the equivalence; the prefix is already regular.
acceptance: This comparison does not apply when the intermediate source is merely CM.

sources.match: This regular-to-regular comparison is the presentation-independence step.

nodes.title: Finite-free resolution bridge
nodes.statement: For a finite module M over a Noetherian local R and n≥0, pd_R M≤n iff there is a native ProjectiveResolution of ModuleCat.of R M with every term finite free and all terms in degrees i>n zero.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Repeatedly choose finite free covers; Noetherianity makes the kernels finite.
Dimension shifting makes the nth kernel projective; finite projective modules over a local ring are free.
Conversely use the exact native resolution and dimension shifting to bound the native projective dimension.
acceptance: For the zero module choose the zero complex; native pd is bottom, not zero.

sources.match: Finite syzygies and local freeness replace arbitrary projective terms.

nodes.title: Minimal finite resolutions
nodes.statement: If R is Noetherian local, M finite and pd_R M≤n, there is such a finite-free native ProjectiveResolution with every differential image contained in m times its target.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Reindex the finite chain complex as a cochain complex supported in degrees −n through 0.
Apply the existing finite minimal representative and transfer its augmentation; the homotopy equivalence preserves H⁰=M.
Reindex back to the native resolution, preserving the degree bound.
acceptance: A nonzero finite free M has a minimal resolution concentrated in degree zero.

sources.match: Cancelling unit pivots yields the minimal resolution used in the depth argument.

nodes.title: Projective dimension from a minimal endpoint
nodes.statement: For a nonzero finite M over a Noetherian local R, if a bounded finite-free minimal native resolution has highest nonzero term in degree n, then pd_R M=n.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the native projective-resolution Ext/cohomology-class comparison to apply Hom_R(−,κ) to the actual resolution. All differentials vanish by minimality, so Ext^n_R(M,κ) is the dual of its nonzero residual nth term.
Nakayama makes this group nonzero. The resolution bound gives pd≤n and the Ext obstruction gives pd≥n.
acceptance: A nonminimal resolution can have a nonzero contractible tail and cannot satisfy this conclusion.

sources.match: Ext detects the last term of a minimal finite resolution.

nodes.title: Depth of nonzero finite free modules
nodes.statement: For a nonzero finite free module F over a Noetherian local R, depth_R F=depth_R R.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Choose a finite basis. A multiplication map on any successive quotient of F is the product of the corresponding multiplication maps on R.
A nonempty basis detects injectivity and a nonzero quotient in both directions, so the sets of regular-list lengths agree.
acceptance: The nonzero hypothesis prevents depth(0)=infinity.

proofSteps: The scalar action on Ext equals precomposition with multiplication by a on its first argument, using bilinearity and the identity class.
Multiplication by a on κ is zero; therefore the induced scalar action is zero.

nodes.title: Minimal maps induce zero on residue Ext
nodes.statement: Let F and G be finite free modules over local R and u:F→G a linear map with image in mG. The induced map Ext^i_R(κ,F)→Ext^i_R(κ,G) is zero for every i.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: In finite bases every matrix entry belongs to m.
Decompose u as a finite sum of a matrix unit times such a scalar. Functor additivity and ext-residue-annihilated kill every summand.

nodes.title: Depth drop for a minimal free injection
nodes.statement: Suppose 0→K→F→M→0 is exact over Noetherian local R, K and F are nonzero finite free, and the first map has image in mF. Then depth_R R≥1 and depth_R M+1=depth_R R.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Let d=depth R, finite by the imported depth bound. For d=0, injectivity of Hom(κ,K)→Hom(κ,F) contradicts its being zero on a nonzero source.
For d>0 all Ext groups below d of K and F vanish, and Ext^d(κ,K) is nonzero.
The zero map Ext^d(κ,K)→Ext^d(κ,F), together with the long exact sequence, makes Ext^(d−1)(κ,M) nonzero and all lower groups zero.
acceptance: An injective minimal map of nonzero finite free modules cannot occur over a depth-zero ring.

sources.match: The Ext characterization and the exact sequence prove the pd-one case without a determinantal criterion.

nodes.title: Depth in a short exact sequence with unequal depths
nodes.statement: In an exact sequence 0→K→F→M→0 of nonzero finite modules over a Noetherian local ring, if depth K<depth F, then depth K≥1 and depth M+1=depth K.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply Ext(κ,−). Below depth K−1 both adjacent groups vanish.
At that degree the connecting map identifies the first nonzero group of K with one for M; if depth K=0, left exactness gives a contradiction.
acceptance: The strict inequality is essential.

sources.match: This is the equality case extracted from the three depth-lemma inequalities.

nodes.title: Auslander–Buchsbaum formula
nodes.statement: Let R be a Noetherian local ring and M a nonzero finite R-module with finite projective dimension. Then pd_R M+depth_R M=depth_R R, using the native projective dimension and the imported depth. In particular pd_R M≤depth R.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Induct on the native finite projective dimension p. The projective case is finite free and uses depth-finite-free.
Use the first syzygy of a minimal resolution. At p=1 apply minimal-free-injection-depth.
At p>1, induction gives depth K=depth R−p+1<depth F; depth-syzygy-strict gives the formula and the necessary nonnegative bound.
acceptance: The zero module is excluded: its native projective dimension is bottom and its depth is infinity.
Over a regular local R, R/(f) for a regular list has pd=f.length and depth=dim R−f.length.

sources.match: The source proves the same formula by regular-element reduction; the packet uses the explicitly decomposed Ext proof.

nodes.title: Projective dimension after killing a common regular element
nodes.statement: Let R be Noetherian local, M nonzero finite with finite pd, and x∈m regular on both R and M. Then pd_(R/xR)(M/xM)=pd_R M.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Tensor a minimal finite free resolution with R/xR. The two-term free resolution of R/xR shows that its positive Tor with M vanishes because x is M-regular.
The resulting resolution is minimal and has the same nonzero endpoint by Nakayama. Apply minimal-resolution-pd.

nodes.title: Syzygy depth bounds
nodes.statement: For a finite module M over a Noetherian local R, let K₀=M and let 0→Kⱼ₊₁→Fⱼ→Kⱼ→0 be any sequence of finite-module exact sequences with Fⱼ finite free. Then depth Kⱼ≥min(depth R, depth M+j), allowing Kⱼ=0 with depth infinity. No finite projective dimension or bounded resolution is assumed; any finite segment suffices for its endpoint bound.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Finite free covers exist for every finite module, and Noetherianity keeps their kernels finite. Iterate only as far as the bound being proved; do not assume termination.
Apply the depth-lemma inequality to each finite syzygy exact sequence.
Keep zero syzygies separate; their infinite depth satisfies the bound.

sources.match: Successive finite free covers improve depth until maximal depth is reached.

nodes.title: Finite projective dimension over regular local rings
nodes.statement: For a regular local R of dimension d and every finite R-module M, pd_R M≤d.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Take d finite free covers. The dth syzygy is zero or has depth at least d, using regular-local CM and the support bound.
The imported freeness-at-maximal-depth theorem makes this syzygy free and terminates the resolution. This proof precedes AB and avoids using it circularly.

nodes.title: Projective dimension of the residue field

nodes.title: Depth bounds for submodules
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local R, a finite module N and nonzero submodule M of N, dim Supp M≥depth N.

Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Choose an associated prime of M; it is also associated to N by the native inclusion theorem.
The imported associated-prime depth bound gives depth N≤dim R/p, and support dimension of M bounds dim R/p.

nodes.title: Depth under a local quotient
nodes.statement: For a surjective local map R→S of Noetherian local rings and finite S-module N, depth_R N=depth_S N.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Lift every list in m_S to m_R. The successive quotient modules and multiplication maps agree under scalar restriction.
Every list in m_R maps to one in m_S; compare the same sets of possible lengths, including infinity for N=0.

nodes.title: Depth under a finite local map
nodes.statement: For a finite local map R→S of Noetherian local rings and a finite S-module N, depth_R N=depth_S N.

Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: A finite algebra over a local ring is semilocal and every maximal ideal lies over m_R.

nodes.title: Depth over a finite semilocal algebra
nodes.statement: Let R be Noetherian local, S a nonzero finite commutative R-algebra, and N a finite S-module. Then depth_(m_R)(N)=min over maximal q of S of depth_(S_q)(N_q), with infinity allowed at zero localizations.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Contraction of associated primes detects depth zero on both sides.
If the minimum is positive, finite prime avoidance chooses an element of m_R regular on N; quotient and induct on the finite minimum.
If N=0 all depths are infinity. Localizations and quotient maps commute with the induction.

nodes.title: Finite image of a compatible ring action
nodes.statement: Let S be Noetherian, M finite over S, and R an S-algebra acting on M compatibly. The image of the action R→End_S(M) is a finite S-algebra, canonically isomorphic to R/Ann_R M.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: The native Noetherian instance makes End_S(M) a finite S-module.
The image is an S-submodule, so it is finite. The kernel of the action is exactly the native annihilator; apply the first isomorphism theorem.
acceptance: R itself need not be finite over S unless its action is faithful.

nodes.title: Depth under a finite action
nodes.statement: Let S→R be a local map of Noetherian local rings and M a nonzero R-module finite over S, with compatible actions. Then depth_S M=depth_R M.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Put T=R/Ann_R M. It is local, finite over S and acts faithfully on M.
Apply depth-finite-local to S→T and depth-surjective-local to R→T.
acceptance: The proof first passes to the action image; finiteness of the whole ring R is not assumed.

Apply the finite local specialization to the action quotient, then compare depths through the surjection.

nodes.title: Support dimension under a finite action
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of depth-finite-action, dim Supp_S M=dim Supp_R M.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: The faithful finite action image T has support dimension dim T on the R side.
The induced S/Ann_S M→T is injective integral finite. Integral dimension comparison identifies its dimension with dim T.
acceptance: Both sides concern support, not the dimension of R.

sources.match: The proof compares dimension through the finite faithful action image.
An injective integral extension preserves Krull dimension; apply this to the base modulo the module annihilator and its action image.

nodes.title: Freeness from a finite CM action
nodes.statement: Let S be regular local and S→R a local map to Noetherian local R. If M is nonzero, finite over S, Cohen–Macaulay over R, and dim Supp_R M=dim S, then M is free over S.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: CM and the dimension hypothesis give depth_R M=dim S. The finite action formula gives the same depth over S.
AB over the regular local S gives pd_S M=0; convert native categorical projectivity to module projectivity, then local finite freeness.
acceptance: This does not require R to be regular or finite over S.

sources.match: This is the module freeness step isolated from the finite-map and faithfulness steps.
Depth and codimension enter derived patching separately.

nodes.title: Faithfulness from an equal-dimensional action
nodes.statement: Let S and R be Noetherian domains of the same finite Krull dimension d, and M a nonzero R-module finite and faithful over S under a compatible S→R action. Then the R action is faithful, and R is finite over S.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: The finite action image T contains S faithfully, so integral dimension comparison gives dim T=dim S=d.
If ker(R→T) were nonzero, every prime chain in R/ker could be enlarged below by the zero prime of R, forcing dim T<dim R.
Thus R→T is an isomorphism and R is finite over S.
acceptance: The domain hypothesis cannot be replaced by equidimensionality alone.

sources.match: A finite action image with the full dimension cannot be a proper quotient of the domain.
The patching ring is identified with its faithful action image by this count.

nodes.title: Kisin’s projective module lemma
nodes.statement: Let S and R be regular Noetherian domains of the same finite Krull dimension d and φ:S→R a ring map. A nonzero R-module M finite projective over S is finite projective and faithful over R; φ is finite.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: A nonzero projective module over a domain is faithful. The equal-dimensional action theorem makes R finite over S and its action faithful.
At q of R over p of S, use the finite completed-algebra product decomposition requested from R03.2: the completed q-localized module is a direct summand of the completed p-localized S-free module.

The isolated completed module is nonzero (M was faithful over R) and finite projective, hence free, over the completed local base. That base is a regular local domain, so it acts faithfully on this module and injects into the finite completed target. Integral dimension comparison equates their local dimensions. Depth-finite-local and AB give freeness over the completed target; descent and local projectivity conclude.
acceptance: Apply only to the regular rings occurring after the source’s scalar inversion.

sources.match: The proof uses completions to isolate the q factor, followed by the depth formula and AB.
Kisin is applied after inverting p; it does not assert integral regularity.

nodes.title: Lifting a fibre nonzerodivisor
nodes.statement: Let R→S be a local map of Noetherian local rings, N finite over S and flat over R. If y∈m_S is injective on N/m_R N, then y is injective on N and N/yN is R-flat.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the local flatness criterion for the map N→N: injectivity on the closed fibre lifts through all m_R-adic quotients.
The separatedness supplied by the native Krull intersection theorem makes the kernel zero. The same criterion identifies its cokernel as R-flat.
acceptance: Finiteness over S is required; arbitrary flat R-modules do not suffice.

sources.match: This is the regular-element lift used in the flat depth induction.

nodes.title: Depth comparison for a depth-zero flat fibre
nodes.statement: For local Noetherian R→S, finite R-module M and finite S-module N flat over R, assume M,N nonzero and depth_(S/m_R S)(N/m_R N)=0. Then depth_S(M⊗R N)=depth_R M.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Induct on depth_R M by a regular element of m_R; R-flatness makes it regular on the tensor product, and both depths fall by one.
At depth_R M=0 embed κ_R into M using its socle. Tensor injectivity embeds N/m_R N, whose depth-zero socle gives depth zero of the tensor product.
acceptance: The tensor product is nonzero by localness, fibre nonvanishing and Nakayama.

sources.locator: §10.163, Lemma10.163.1, tag0338, pp.452–453, depth-zero fibre case
sources.match: A socle injection supplies the base case of the tensor depth formula.

nodes.title: Depth formula for flat tensor products
nodes.statement: Let R→S be a local map of Noetherian local rings, M a nonzero finite R-module and N a nonzero finite S-module flat over R. Then depth_S(M⊗R N)=depth_R M+depth_(S/m_R S)(N/m_R N).
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Induct on the finite depth of N/m_R N. Lift a first fibre regular element with flat-fibre-regular-lift.
The local flatness criterion makes the same y regular on M⊗N and identifies its quotient with M⊗(N/yN).
Apply induction and the regular-element depth drop.
acceptance: Taking M=R and N=S gives the ring depth formula; this is not a formula for arbitrary nonflat maps.

sources.match: The statement keeps both coefficient modules and the closed-fibre module explicit.

nodes.title: Depth of a flat local ring map
nodes.statement: For a flat local map of Noetherian local rings R→S, depth S=depth R+depth(S/m_R S).
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.

acceptance: If the closed fibre is a field, the two ring depths agree.

nodes.title: Cohen–Macaulayness under a flat local map
nodes.statement: For a flat local map of Noetherian local rings R→S, S is Cohen–Macaulay iff R and S/m_R S are Cohen–Macaulay.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: The two depths add by flat-local-ring-depth; the two dimensions add by the native going-down height formula at the maximal ideals.
Each depth is at most its dimension. Equality of the sums holds exactly when equality holds in both factors.

nodes.title: Depth under local completion

Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.

The closed fibre of the completed ring is κ_R of depth zero; the tensor formula proves equality.

nodes.title: Lifting conormal generators
nodes.statement: For Noetherian local R, I⊆m_R, and elements f₁,…,f_c in I, if their classes generate the native conormal I/I² over R/I, then they generate I.

nodes.statement: Let R be Noetherian local and I⊆J⊆m_R. If R/J has finite projective dimension over R/I, then I∩m_R J=m_R I, equivalently I/m_R I→J/m_R J is injective.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: If a nonzero class f in I/mI maps to zero, choose I′ containing mI with I/I′ spanned by f.
R/I′→R/I is a principal square-zero extension; writing f as a relation in mJ gives a nonnilpotent obstruction class.
The exact missing Tate-resolution obstruction is recorded as a gap, not assumed as an unproved generic vanishing theorem.
acceptance: For the finite module R/J over Noetherian local R/I, finite Tor dimension and finite pd agree. This finite-pd formulation uses the native dimension carrier.

sources.match: The square-zero obstruction forces unbounded even Tor if the conormal map is not injective.

nodes.title: Nested ideals of finite Tor dimension
nodes.statement: Let R be Noetherian local, I⊆J⊆m_R, J a regular-sequence ideal, and R/J of finite projective dimension over R/I. Then I is a regular-sequence ideal and J/I is a regular-sequence ideal in R/I.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Extend a residue basis of I/mI to one of J/mJ, using the injection. Lift the basis so its prefix generates I.
The full list is regular by regular-sequence-ideal-minimal-generators; its prefix and the quotient tail are regular by the native list recursion.
acceptance: Both ideals are proper and the quotient ideal is the actual image.

sources.match: The conormal injection permits a minimal generator list with the desired prefix.

nodes.title: Regular ideals across a flat regular fibre
nodes.statement: Let R→S be flat local Noetherian with regular closed fibre, I⊆m_R, J⊆m_S and IS⊆J. Assume the induced quotient map R/I→S/J is flat. Then J is a regular-sequence ideal iff I is a regular-sequence ideal and J/IS is one in S/IS.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply relative-flat-module-pd to R/I→S/IS and N=S/J: the hypothesis is flatness of the actual induced quotient map, and the closed fibre is the same regular ring.
Use nested-regular-ideals in S with IS⊆J. Faithful-flat descent gives regularity of I.
In the converse direction concatenate a regular generator list of IS and a lifted regular list for J/IS.
acceptance: The closed fibre must be regular; CM alone does not supply this transfer.

sources.match: The Tor transfer and nested-ideal lemma give the two regular ideals.

nodes.title: Avramov’s flat local CI criterion
nodes.statement: For a flat local map R→S of Noetherian local rings, S is local CI iff R and S/m_R S are local CI.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Complete both rings and use the requested regular presentation diagram R₀→S₀ with flat regular closed fibre and horizontal quotient maps.
For kernels I and J use flat-regular-fibre-ideals; flatness of R→S provides Tor dimension zero.

Identify the minimal generators of J/IS₀ with those of the closed-fibre kernel. Native dimension addition and the conormal criterion give the forward implication; lifting fibre regular elements gives the reverse.
acceptance: No excellence hypothesis is required for this absolute ring theorem.

sources.locator: §23.8, Proposition23.8.4 and Lemma23.8.9, tags09Q2 and09Q7, pp.21–22
sources.match: The base and fibre equivalence is Avramov’s theorem, not an elementary consequence of depth.

nodes.title: Localization of local CI rings
nodes.statement: If R is Noetherian local CI and p a prime ideal, then R_p is local CI.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Choose a prime of R̂ lying over p by faithful flatness. The flat local CI criterion descends along R_p→(R̂)_q.

For the complete case use a regular presentation and localize its regular list inside the prime. Regularity of the localized source is the explicit regular-local prime-localization gap; the current upstream4D text does not itself supply that general ring theorem.
acceptance: Do not infer a corresponding localization statement for arbitrary completed lci morphisms.

sources.match: Descent from a prime of the completion reduces to localizing the regular quotient presentation.

nodes.title: Detection of global local CI at maximal ideals
nodes.statement: For Noetherian R, IsLocallyCompleteIntersection R iff R_m is local CI for every maximal ideal m.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: A prime lies below a maximal ideal. Localize the local CI maximal localization once more and identify the resulting ring with R_p.
acceptance: The global zero-ring case is vacuous on both sides.

sources.match: Localization stability reduces the global quantifier to maximal ideals.

nodes.title: Local CI rings are Cohen–Macaulay
nodes.statement: Every Noetherian local CI ring R is Cohen–Macaulay.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: The completion is a regular local ring modulo a regular sequence, hence CM by iterated regular-quotient CM invariance.
Its closed fibre over R is the residue field. Descend CM by the flat local CM equivalence.
acceptance: CM does not imply CI: k[[X,Y]]/(X,Y)² is a zero-dimensional counterexample.

sources.match: Use a regular-sequence presentation of the completion in the absolute CI definition.
A regular-sequence quotient of a regular local ring is CM, and flat-local CM descent applies to the completion map.

nodes.title: The tangent cone of a regular local ring
nodes.statement: Let R be regular local of dimension d and f:Fin d→m_R a minimal generator family. The existing P7 polynomial map ε_f:(R/m_R)[X₁,…,X_d]→Gr_m R is an isomorphism of graded algebras; it sends X_i to the existing degree-one class of f_i.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the existing surjective graded polynomial map on the ordinary Rees quotient.

The Hilbert–Samuel dimension comparison gives degree d−1 for graded-piece growth when d>0. A nonzero homogeneous kernel relation would force smaller growth; the exact polynomial-quotient counting leaf remains a gap.
Handle d=0 separately: m=0 and the degree-zero field map is an isomorphism.
acceptance: The source is not merely a polynomial surjection; injectivity is what supplies the domain proof.

sources.match: The proof compares Hilbert growth to rule out any homogeneous relation.

nodes.title: Regular local rings are domains
nodes.statement: Every regular local ring R is a domain.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: For nonzero a and b, native Krull intersection gives finite maximal m-adic orders.
Their initial forms in the actual P7 tangent cone are nonzero. The polynomial-algebra comparison makes their product nonzero, so ab cannot vanish.
acceptance: This closes the statement inventory of the precise domain leaf recorded by P7, without asserting its Hilbert–Samuel proof is closed.

sources.match: Separatedness and the polynomial tangent cone prove absence of zero divisors.

nodes.title: Freeness from a free closed fibre
nodes.statement: Let R→S be a flat local map of Noetherian local rings, N a finite S-module flat over R. If N/m_R N is free over S/m_R S, then N is free over S.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Lift a finite fibre basis to N. Nakayama gives a surjection S^r→N with finite kernel K.
R-flatness of N preserves the kernel exact sequence on tensoring with κ_R. The fibre map is an isomorphism, so K/m_R K=0.
Since m_R S⊆m_S, Nakayama gives K=0.
acceptance: N=0 is permitted and is free with empty basis.

sources.match: The finite cover and exact fibre comparison give the module form of the local flatness argument.

nodes.title: Finite pd across a regular closed fibre
nodes.statement: For a flat local Noetherian map R→S with regular closed fibre of dimension d, every finite S-module N flat over R has pd_S N≤d.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Take d finite S-free covers. Their kernels stay R-flat, since the successive quotient modules are R-flat.
On the closed fibre these become an exact free resolution; its dth syzygy is free over the regular local closed fibre.
Apply relative-flat-module-free to the dth syzygy and terminate.
acceptance: The dimension bound is the closed-fibre dimension, not dim R.

sources.locator: §15.79, Lemma15.79.6, tag09PC, pp.203–204, tor-amplitude[0,0] module case
sources.match: This isolates the flat-module case used by the CI proof and avoids a general Tor transfer predicate.

nodes.title: Associated primes under scalar restriction
nodes.statement: Let R→S be a ring map with S Noetherian and N an S-module, with the induced compatible R action. The R-associated primes of N are exactly the contractions of its S-associated primes. Neither a finite map nor a finite module is required. Here associated primes means the native Mathlib radical-annihilator predicate; for Noetherian rings it agrees with the usual annihilator definition.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: Contraction of the radical annihilator of an element commutes with scalar restriction, giving one inclusion.

For an R-associated element z, let L be its cyclic S-submodule and I its S-annihilator. Its R-annihilator has the associated prime as radical. The native minimal-prime lifting theorem finds a minimal prime over I contracting to that prime.
The Noetherian cyclic module S/I has that minimal prime associated; its injection into N and native associated-prime inclusion give the reverse inclusion.
acceptance: Noetherianity of S supplies association of minimal primes in the cyclic S-module used in the reverse inclusion. The statement makes no claim for an arbitrary non-Noetherian S.
When R is non-Noetherian, use the literal native radical-annihilator convention; the source’s example with infinitely many square-zero variables is not a counterexample for that convention.

sources.match: The cyclic-submodule and minimal-prime argument proves the stated comparison. With non-Noetherian R the packet uses the native radical-annihilator variant; the same argument starts from a minimal prime over the contracted annihilator.

nodes.title: The fibre injection criterion
nodes.statement: Let R→S be a local map of Noetherian local rings, N a finite S-module and P a flat R-module. For an R-linear map u:N→P, injectivity of its actual reduction N/m_R N→P/m_R P implies injectivity of u and R-flatness of coker u. P need not be finite or an S-module.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity; module actions and scalar towers are compatible.
Finiteness, localness, nonzero conditions and map hypotheses are exactly those in the statement.
proofSteps: R-flatness of P identifies its m_R-adic graded pieces with the corresponding coefficient pieces tensored with its closed fibre. Fibre injectivity therefore places ker(u) in every m_R-adic power of N.
The native separatedness theorem for the finite S-module N kills this kernel, since m_R S lies inside m_S.

Repeat the injectivity argument over R/a for each ideal a: P/aP is flat, the closed fibre map is unchanged, and N/aN is finite over S/aS. The resulting injection N/aN→P/aP makes the cokernel R-flat by the ideal tensor criterion.
acceptance: The finite S-module and local-map conditions supply separatedness; injectivity on a fibre alone does not suffice for arbitrary modules.

sources.match: Adic separatedness lifts fibre injectivity, and reduction by every ideal tests cokernel flatness.

The general regular-local prime-localization theorem needed for ci-localization is a separate recorded gap, not a verified upstream4D contract.
